items.title: WildBotics Training
items.text:
Autonomous Sampling with Robotics in the Wild for Nature Conservation. An EU Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network of twelve doctoral candidates, twelve beneficiaries and nine associated partners across Europe, Kenya and Greenland, running from 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2029.

This site holds the network's training materials, the WildBotics Summer School, and resources for the people working in the network.

Find out more at WildBotics.eu

items.title: About WildBotics
items.text:
Autonomous Sampling with Robotics in the Wild for Nature Conservation

Earth is losing biodiversity faster than ever, and conservation needs practices that are effective and affordable. Much of today's conservation work, from collecting samples to inspecting and monitoring wildlife and habitats, is labour-intensive, costly and slow, and the data it produces can be incomplete or biased. Advances in robotics and artificial intelligence now offer conservationists practical new tools.

WildBotics brings robotics, sensing and AI together with conservation ecology. Autonomous aerial, ground and aquatic robots are the common platform for new long-endurance systems, better sensors and software, and automated ways of monitoring wildlife and ecosystems and of collecting and interpreting samples at scale.

items.title: A doctoral network
items.text:
WildBotics trains a new generation of researchers who can work across engineering, computer science and ecology. Its doctoral candidates are hosted by universities, research institutes and companies across Europe, and work alongside conservation organisations in Europe, Africa and the Arctic. Their training programme combines research, scientific and technical, and transferable skills with fieldwork, hackathons and a summer school.

Visit WildBotics.eu

items.title: Building on WildDrone
items.text:
WildBotics builds on the groundwork laid by WildDrone, the MSCA Doctoral Network on autonomous drones for nature conservation, and on the lessons learned there. WildDrone's research, training and fieldwork with conservation partners shaped how WildBotics is designed, and the two networks (via WildDrone's ongoing post-funding community) continue to meet and work together. WildDrone's papers, deliverables and other results are on its outputs page.

Visit WildDrone.eu WildDrone outputs

items.title: WildBotics Summer School
items.text:
When June 2028, one week Where Universidad de Salamanca, Spain Who Open to researchers from outside the network, as well as WildBotics DCs Organisers USAL, with BioConsult SH

A week on the theory and practice of robotics for conservation fieldwork. Invited speakers give tutorials on aerial, ground and aquatic robots, sensing and AI for ecology and conservation. WildBotics doctoral candidates run mini-courses for participants from outside the network and present their results.

Details to follow

The programme, speakers, how to apply and practical information will be published here well ahead of the school. Proceedings, including talks, slides and posters, will be published here afterwards. The dates and venue are provisional until then.

items.title: Credit
items.text:
Doctoral candidates can earn ECTS for the summer school, whether or not they are part of WildBotics. Everyone who attends is credited for attending: there is no report to submit. Details of the credit available will be published with the programme.

For WildBotics DCs the school is module S11, part of the M30 training event.
